title: Wren and the Deadline
premise: August Crane, a hostage negotiator haunted by the one exchange that ended in blood, is approached by a stranger named Wren who claims August once saved her life — a favor August never performed. Wren's 'interest' on the phantom debt is simple: help extract Dr. Ilya Sorensen, a defector carrying proof that a summit security chief sold the venue's blueprints, before the summit convenes in six days. As August and Wren run the extraction, they discover Sorensen himself is the bait in a trap meant to flush out every compromised negotiator in the service — including August's mentor. In the end, August trades their polished lie for the truth on an open channel, letting themselves be taken so Wren can deliver Sorensen and the evidence, choosing love against duty at the exact moment duty demands silence.
about_author: Xanthe Almeida is the pen name of a former crisis-line counselor who spent seven years listening to strangers talk each other back from ledges. They write thrillers about people who negotiate for a living and fail to negotiate with themselves.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: POV: August. August Crane talks a bank gunman down in eleven minutes flat, then comes home to a packed go-bag and a rehearsed lie about where they were last Tuesday. A note under the door reads: 'You saved my life. Time to repay it. Midnight.' The beat: competence as armor, and the first hairline crack in it.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: POV: August. At midnight, Wren appears — sharp, calm, holding a file August never wrote about an incident August doesn't remember. She names her price: help extract defector Dr. Ilya Sorensen from a safehouse in Riga before the summit convenes. August refuses; she leaves the file anyway. Beat: curiosity curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: POV: August, with a Wren interlude. August verifies the file: Sorensen is real, the summit security chief's signature is on documents he should never have touched. August's mentor, Director Hale, warns them off the case in a way that confirms it. Beat: the moment refusing becomes impossible.

chapters.title: Riga Rules
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Wren runs the approach to the safehouse while August works the human angle — talking past Sorensen's armed handlers using pure negotiation craft. They get Sorensen moving, but a second team shadows them, too disciplined to be criminals. Beat: wary partnership becoming something warmer under pressure.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: POV: August. Sorensen admits he may be bait: his defection was too easy, his handlers too thin. If he's a lure, someone wanted Western negotiators pulled into the open — and August realizes the trap isn't for Sorensen. It's for people like August. Beat: paranoia reframing everything already done.

chapters.title: Hale's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Digging into who benefits, Wren finds Hale's name threaded through the compromised channels — August's mentor, the man who taught August to keep a lie polished. Confronting August with it nearly breaks the partnership. Beat: loyalty and evidence at war; love against duty begins to bite.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: POV: August. Ambushed at a border crossing, August negotiates their way out by feeding the ambushers a false route — buying hours but burning their cover with the service. Hale calls personally, offering absolution if August walks away. Beat: the polished lie offered back at full price.

chapters.title: What the Debt Was
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Wren confesses: there was no favor. She manufactured the debt because August was the only negotiator clean enough — and stubborn enough — to survive what she knew was coming. August, furious, chooses to stay anyway. Beat: the relationship rebuilt on truth instead of gratitude.

chapters.title: The Summit Floor
chapters.summary: POV: August. Climax. With hours left, August walks into the summit perimeter and opens a channel everyone can hear, laying out Hale's ledger live — trading their own career, freedom, and safety as the distraction while Wren moves Sorensen and the evidence through the chaos. Beat: justice outside the law, paid for inside it.

chapters.title: After the Exchange
chapters.summary: POV: August, closing with Wren. Hale is arrested; August sits in a hearing room answering for methods no regulation covers. Weeks later, released with a suspended badge, August finds Wren waiting with two coffees and no debts between them. The go-bag stays unpacked. Beat: resolution — duty survived, love chosen, the lie finally retired.
